correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier transform of [-1,1]^n reduces H_{p,u}(R) to (p 2^n/prod_j a_j^2) int_0^R prod_j sin²(a_j r) r^{p-2k-1} dr, where k is number of nonzero coordinates. The finite trigonometric polynomial has positive mean M=4^-k sum_lambda C_lambda², so for p=2k the integral grows M log R+O(1), for p>2k it grows M R^{p-2k}/(p-2k), and it converges exactly for p<2k. AM–GM on sin² terms gives M≤binom(2k,k)/4^k; strict equality rigidity follows because nonidentical positive frequencies give nonzero nonnegative trigonometric gap with strictly positive time mean. For k=3 signed resonance enumeration gives M=1/8+E/16−T/32 and precisely five values 3/32,1/8,5/32,3/16,5/16. Independently enumerated 729 positive integer triples and reproduced all five cases and bounds, supporting but not proving unrestricted real frequencies. No uniform near-resonance error is claimed.
